q.line: I'm on a shoulder of lemon fields
stanza: It finally hits me, a mile's drive
The sky is leaking, my windshield's cryin'
I'm feeling sacred, my soul is stripped
Radio's painful, the words are clipped
The grief, it gets me, the weird goodbyes
My car is creeping, I think it's dyin'
I'm pulling over until it heals
I'm on a shoulder of lemon fields

partner.line: I'm pulling over until it heals

q.line: And ghostly voices rose from the fields
stanza: I heard the wind rustling through the trees
And ghostly voices rose from the fields
I ran with my heart pounding down that broken path
With the devil snappin' at my heels

partner.line: I heard the wind rustling through the trees

q.line: Looking back at the years gone by like so many summer fields
stanza: Looking out at the road rushing under my wheels
Looking back at the years gone by like so many summer fields
In '65, I was seventeen and running up 101
I don't know where I'm running now, I'm just running on

partner.line: Looking out at the road rushing under my wheels

q.line: In dirt in other potter's fields
stanza: Interred with other daughters
In dirt in other potter's fields
Above them, parades
Mark the passing of days
Through parks where pale colonnades arch in marble and steel

partner.line: Through parks where pale colonnades arch in marble and steel

q.line: I told you about Strawberry Fields
stanza: I told you about Strawberry Fields
You know the place where nothing is real
Well, here's another place you can go
Where everything flows

partner.line: You know the place where nothing is real

stanza: Let me take you down, 'cause I'm going to
Strawberry Fields
Nothing is real
And nothing to get hung about
Strawberry Fields forever

q.line: And rolls along past houses, farms and fields
stanza: Riding on the City of New Orleans
Illinois Central, Monday morning rail
Fifteen cars and fifteen restless riders
Three conductors and twenty-five sacks of mail
All along the southbound odyssey
The train pulls out at Kankakee
And rolls along past houses, farms and fields
Passing trains that have no name
And freight yards full of old black men
And the graveyards of the rusted automobiles

partner.line: And the graveyards of the rusted automobiles

q.line: Ten years old in the killing fields
stanza: I am in this God forsaken place
While baby wipes the dirt from the little one's face
Ten years old in the killing fields
Baby's planning the weekly meals
Took a Flintstone pill, pantry uphill
Curtain child within my teens, our dreams
Ride through Hyrule fields
Roaming, scuffin'
Mileage on my bike breezing

partner.line: Curtain child within my teens, our dreams

stanza: I began to warm and chill
To objects and their fields
A ragged cup, a twisted mop
The face of Jesus in my soup
Those sinister dinner deals
The meal trolley's wicked wheels
A hooked bone rising from my food
All things either good or ungood

q.songTitle: For Emily, Whenever I May Find Her
stanza: And when you ran to me
Your cheeks flushed with the night
We walked on frosted fields
Of juniper and lamplight
I held your hand

partner.line: And when you ran to me

stanza: Saw your face carved in the caves
In the tunneling fields
I wore my stubbornness like armor
A reliable shield
Birds in the sky
Birds in the eaves
In the leaves
In the fields
In the castles and ponds...
Corn in the fields
Listen to the rice when the wind blows 'cross the water
F/a fm/abc
